Article Title: 'Incredibly proud': SpiceJet lauds Captain Smit Machchhar, who flew with airline for 11 years
Article Text:
Smit Machchhar

NEW DELHI: SpiceJet, the Gurugram-based budget carrier and former employer of Captain Smit Machchhar, on Thursday praised the pilot after he was stabbed by his co-pilot aboard an Israel-bound flight but managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers to enter and overpower the attacker.Chairman and Managing Director Ajay Singh said that "all of India and SpiceJet" is "incredibly proud of him.""I was incredibly proud to know of this, but this is the job of a pilot. His job is to protect the lives that have been entrusted to him. And in this case, 180 lives were entrusted to Captain Smit Machchhar, and he did a tremendous job saving and preserving those lives. So really incredibly proud of him. All of SpiceJet is proud of him, and of course, all of India is proud of him," Singh told ANI."The first thing that will go through a pilot's mind is preserving lives, saving lives. And remember that in this case, what really saved lives was the fact that he was able to open the door of that cockpit, and let me tell you that the handle which allows that door to be opened is actually on the co-pilot's side. So, it would have needed real courage, after being stabbed, to reach out to the co-pilot side and somehow find a way to unlatch that door.So the fact that he was able to do it essentially saved those lives because then passengers and other pilots were able to come into the cockpit and help him overpower the co-pilot and fly the plane back," he added.The captain was also able to activate the cockpit door emergency release mechanism, communicate with the crew on board and send an emergency communication signal."The mechanics are that the cabin crew or anybody on the outside can punch a code in that door. But the door still doesn't open. It needs the captain to physically unlock the door. And that unlocking mechanism is actually on the side of the co-pilot. In this case, the co-pilot was actually attacking the captain, and he still managed to reach out and find a way to unlock that door. And that is possibly what saved lives," the SpiceJet chairman and managing director said.Machchhar, who spent 11 years with SpiceJet, has more than 13 years of commercial aviation experience and has logged 9,750 flying hours, primarily operating Boeing 737 aircraft. He later joined UAE-based airline flydubai, where he currently serves.On Wednesday, the flight was en route from Dubai to Israel's Tel Aviv when Machchhar was stabbed by the co-pilot, reportedly an Omani national. The flight was later diverted to Saudi Arabia's Tabluk, where it made an emergency landing. Around 180 passengers, mostly Israelis, were on board.Machchhar is currently recovering at a hospital in the kingdom and is in stable condition, according to the Indian Embassy in Riyadh.
Article Summary: Smit machchhar was stabbed by his co-pilot aboard an israel-bound flight. He managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers to enter and overpower the attacker. Spicejet chairman and managing director ajay singh said that "all of india and spicejet" is "incredibly proud of him"

Article Title: Flydubai flight drama: How Indian pilot Smit Machchhar stopped Omani co-pilot from crashing plane
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: An Indian pilot has been identified as the captain who helped prevent a flydubai passenger plane from crashing after his co-pilot allegedly tried to take control of the aircraft during a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, according to Israeli media reports and an Israeli journalist.The Indian pilot has been identified as Captain Smit Machchhar, based in Dubai, who intervened to stop his Omani co-pilot allegedly trying to take control of the aircraft and crash it.The Indian captain was stabbed repeatedly and drenched in blood, according to various witness reports and officials.Machchhar is an experienced commercial pilot with more than 13 years of flying experience on Boeing 737 aircraft. He has been a captain with flydubai since June 2022, having previously spent 11 years with SpiceJet, where he served as a senior commander and Line Training Captain.During his time at SpiceJet, Machchhar reportedly flew more than 9,500 hours, including over 6,400 hours as pilot-in-command, and served as a Line Training Captain from November 2020 to June 2022. His experience includes pilot training and mentoring, crew resource management, flight standards and compliance, and B737 NG and MAX operations.The incident unfolded aboard flydubai Flight FZ1073 on Wednesday, with the Boeing 737 sending emergency signals before making an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. The flight was carrying around 180 Israeli passengers, all of whom were reported safe.Also read: Passengers recall harrowing ordeal on flight that nearly crashed The flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv was flying over Jordan when it transmitted an emergency signal, followed by another signal indicating possible unlawful interference.Israeli officials said the emergency signals followed a physical altercation between the two pilots. Reuters reported that the co-pilot was believed to have stabbed the captain before cabin crew entered the cockpit. Both pilots were later hospitalised after the aircraft landed in Tabuk.Israeli media reports said the suspected attacker attempted to take control of the aircraft and force it into a descent. Passengers reportedly heard screaming and saw blood inside the cockpit.Flight-tracking data showed the aircraft plunging rapidly from around 34,000 feet to about 20,000 feet, with Reuters reporting a drop of nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds before the aircraft stabilised.The aircraft was initially treated as a possible hijacking, prompting Israeli fighter jets to be scrambled. The Israeli prime minister's office later said the incident was not believed to have been a hijacking.Israeli media reports have described the incident as a possible attempted suicide or deliberate crash, while Israeli officials cited by Reuters said they were assessing it as a possible attempted "terror attack". Reuters also reported that officials did not believe the incident was related to a mental-health issue.Later, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the pilots became involved in a physical altercation as the flight approached Israel. “During the flight as they approached the country one of the pilots stabbed the other pilot,” Netanyahu said in a video address.“Apparently he tried to crash the plane with its occupants.” Netanyahu added “almost all” passengers were Israelis, with some passengers and crew members breaking into the cockpit and subduing the attacker. “I spoke with one of the Israeli passengers. He told me that the plane went into a spin and began to dive. He told me that somehow he managed to break into the cockpit with one of the crew members and together they neutralized the stabbing pilot while he was trying to sabotage the aircraft’s systems,” Netanyahu said. “Another air crew that was on the plane entered the cockpit and managed to stabilize the plane,” he added. He also praised those who intervened, saying: “I salute these heroes who showed exceptional resourcefulness and courage.They saved many lives and prevented a major disaster.”Also read: Israel security minister on flydubai cockpit incident Flydubai has confirmed that Flight FZ1073 experienced an incident during its journey from Dubai to Tel Aviv and diverted to Tabuk, where it landed safely."Our teams are working closely with the relevant authorities. Further updates will be issued as additional confirmed details become available," the airline said.Read more: Passenger's mother says pilot tried to kill co-pilot on Flydubai flight The airline has not publicly confirmed the identities or nationalities of the pilots or provided details about what happened inside the cockpit.The investigation is continuing, with Israeli authorities examining the circumstances of the cockpit confrontation, the alleged attempt to take control of the aircraft and the security clearance given to the crew.
Article Summary: The indian pilot has been identified as captain smit machchhar, based in dubai. He intervened to stop his omani co-pilot allegedly trying to take control of the aircraft and crash it. The captain has years of experience and was a spicejet pilot till 2022.

NEW DELHI: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Wednesday praised Indian flydubai pilot Captain Smit Machchhar for his bravery after he was seriously injured in a cockpit altercation that forced a Dubai-Tel Aviv flight to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. Netanyahu met passengers after they returned to Israel and said the actions of Machchhar, passengers and crew had helped avert a major disaster.“My salute to the Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar for his extraordinary bravery. Despite being stabbed and seriously injured, he fought back, resisted, opened the cockpit door, and enabled passengers and crew to overpower the attacker — preventing a catastrophic mid-air disaster,” Netanyahu said in a post.“He saved the lives of 174 people, including Israeli citizens and other nationals. I wish Captain Machchhar a speedy and full recovery. He is a true hero,” he said.The Indian Embassy in Riyadh said Machchhar was receiving treatment at a hospital in Tabuk and was in stable condition.“Our Embassy in Riyadh and Consulate in Jeddah have been following the health condition of Mr Smit Machchhar, the brave Indian pilot of Flydubai flight that was diverted to Tabuk today,” it said in a post on X.“A full update on his health is awaited but he is reported to be in stable condition,” the embassy said, adding that it was in contact with his family and Saudi authorities.The embassy said it would continue to follow up on his health and provide all possible assistance for his wellbeing.Netanyahu met passengers after a rescue flight carrying around 180 people, most of them Israelis, landed at Ben Gurion International Airport.Describing the episode as an “extremely serious security incident”, Netanyahu praised the passengers and crew members who intervened during the flight. He said they had shown “exceptional resourcefulness and courage” and “saved many lives” by preventing what he described as a major disaster.Netanyahu also said the pilot accused of attacking the other pilot had been arrested and was being interrogated by Saudi authorities.Israeli passenger Yaniv, who was among those who intervened, later told Netanyahu that he entered the cockpit and found the alleged attacker at the aircraft's controls.“When I went in, I saw the terrorist on the controls, between the two seats. There were no pilots in the seats,” Yaniv said, according to The Times of Israel.He said he pulled the man away from the controls and called on other passengers to restrain him. When he realised the aircraft was tilting sharply, Yaniv said he returned to the cockpit and pulled back on the controls until the aircraft began to level out.He said he knew what to do because “I watch Mayday”, referring to the aviation accident documentary series.“The plane started leveling out a little more, and then the pilot told me he was taking over from there,” he said.Another passenger, Tzika Manes, told Israel's Channel 12 that he and two other Israeli passengers helped subdue the alleged attacker.Manes said his wife had heard screams and sounds of a struggle near the cockpit and alerted a flight attendant. He said passengers were thrown around the cabin as the aircraft lost altitude.The three passengers eventually restrained the alleged attacker using corded headphones, with the effort taking around 20 to 25 minutes, according to Manes.A doctor travelling on the flight also helped treat the injured pilot, he said.The flydubai flight was diverted to Tabuk in north-western Saudi Arabia and made an emergency landing there.The passengers were subsequently flown back to Israel on a rescue flight. The Israel Airports Authority had earlier set up a dedicated waiting and information area at Ben Gurion Airport for relatives of those on board.Netanyahu's office said the situation had been brought under control and that Israeli authorities were working to ensure the passengers' safe return.Israel scrambled fighter jets after concerns that the aircraft could have been hijacked, according to reports citing Israeli officials.The incident prompted security consultations in Israel, while authorities maintained contact with Saudi officials over the passengers and the investigation.An Israeli official described the episode as a “severe disaster” that had been averted.Flydubai confirmed that flight FZ1073, travelling from Dubai International Airport to Ben Gurion Airport, had experienced an incident and landed safely in Tabuk.“Our teams are working closely with the relevant authorities,” the airline said.The airline did not provide details of the cockpit altercation.The incident involved an altercation between the pilots while the aircraft was travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv.An Israeli official told AP that one of the pilots was armed with a knife. Reuters reported that the co-pilot was believed to have stabbed the captain before cabin crew entered the cockpit.The captain and first officer were injured and taken to hospital, according to Tabuk airport authorities cited by Saudi state television.Netanyahu said the evidence indicated that one pilot had stabbed the other and apparently attempted to crash the aircraft.Publicly available flight-tracking data showed that the aircraft transmitted an emergency alert around two-and-a-half hours after departing Dubai and subsequently dropped sharply from about 33,000 feet to 17,000 feet within roughly a minute before making an erratic turn near the Jordanian border.The circumstances of the cockpit altercation remain under investigation.Saudi authorities are questioning the alleged attacker, while Israeli authorities are examining the security implications of the incident and are expected to question passengers after their return.Transport minister Miri Regev asked Israel's Civil Aviation Authority to investigate what she described as an alleged violation of the aviation agreement between Israel and the UAE. She also called for flydubai flights to Israel to be suspended.Israeli media reported that Machchhar was of Indian origin and that the other pilot was reportedly Omani. Those nationality details had not been independently confirmed by flydubai.Reports also said a second team of pilots in civilian clothes was aboard the aircraft and helped prevent one of the pilots from taking control, though that detail had not been independently confirmed.The investigation remains underway, with flydubai saying it is working with the relevant authorities.

NEW DELHI: The INDIA bloc on Wednesday announced a series of nationwide protests against the Election Commission and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, seeking to project opposition unity amid the ongoing row over voter rolls.Addressing a press conference after the INDIA bloc meeting, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the alliance would hold district-level “Save Democracy” marches and demonstrations outside district magistrate offices from October 2 to 8.“From October 2 to 8, we will hold district-level 'Save Democracy' marches and stage demonstrations outside the offices of every district magistrate. We will also make people aware of why we are undertaking this campaign,” Kharge said.He said all opposition MPs would march to the Election Commission on October 6. Kharge said the opposition had initially planned to hold the march on Wednesday but decided to organise it later with greater participation.“On October 6, all opposition MPs will march to the Election Commission. We wanted to go today itself, but we decided to call the MPs again and organise the protest properly, so we have fixed October 6 for the march,” he said.Kharge added that Rajya Sabha members and MPs from all parties, as well as those who wanted to “protect democracy in the country”, would be invited to join the march.The alliance also plans to seek an appointment with President Droupadi Murmu in the second week of October. Leaders of the opposition will submit a representation outlining what Kharge described as the difficulties they were facing and the constitutional issues involved.A fourth phase of the campaign will comprise five major rallies, with their dates and venues to be announced later.The INDIA bloc meeting also saw Kharge reiterate his criticism of the Election Commission and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. He alleged that the poll panel was being influenced by the government and said the parties had agreed to fight the issue together.“From October 2 to 8, we will hold district-level 'Save Democracy' marches and stage demonstrations outside the offices of every District Magistrate. We will also make people aware of why we are undertaking this campaign,” Kharge said.Addressing the briefing, ex-Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee lashed out at the CEC and call on him to resign."He (CEC Gyanesh Kumar) must resign immediately. Let us save the democracy and make the security of the people, the voting rights... It is our constitutional rights. It is our obligation to the people. If people are not voting, if their voting are been looted and cheated, then where the country will go? So, our request...it our demand. Our forceful demand," the former Bengal CM said.The opposition has demanded a rollback of the SIR exercise, greater transparency in electoral rolls and safeguards against the exclusion of eligible voters. Kharge also called for the use of pre-SIR electoral rolls for future elections and sought prior notice, reasons and an effective appeal mechanism before legitimate voters are removed.The meeting was attended by representatives of Congress, SP, AITC, NCP(SP), SS (UBT), RJD, CPM, CPI, JKNC, JKPDP, JMM, CPI-ML, IUML, KC(M), MDMK, VCK, RSP, KC(J) and AIFB.

NEW DELHI: The INDIA bloc, led by the Congress, has announced a mega action plan to take forward its campaign against “vote chori” and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The key stakeholders of the INDIA bloc met today in the national capital to chalk out a roadmap for nationwide protests against the Election Commission’s “flawed and partisan” approach.The INDIA bloc's renewed offensive comes days after an Indian Express report citing internal differences within the Election Commission of India (ECI) regarding the implementation of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and modifications to voter registration processes. The opposition parties' meeting also comes in the backdrop of successful mobilisation programmed led by the Cockroach Janata Party against NEET paper leak, which brought the GenZ to the streets and forced the government to accept their demands.After hours long deliberations, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge unveiled the opposition’s blueprint for intensified demonstrations against EC’s ‘malpractices’ and shared details of how the INDIA bloc will stand up against electoral irregularities.Here is what the INDIA bloc allies decided on their action plan against EC’s ‘partisan approach and malpractices’Then there was also a list of 6 demands which the opposition parties announced. It includedSo far, so good. But the problem is that all these demands have already been raised by various opposition parties from time to time without any success.We have heard several leaders in the past demanding a return to ballot paper. This has not happened and is unlikely to happen.The fight over alleged discrepancies in the SIR process has been an ongoing one. We have seen Rahul Gandhi and other regional leaders raise the issue. But none of them have managed to sustain the momentum or stop the process. Even the courts have refused to back their allegations and have not stopped the SIR process.Now, let’s focus on the action plan.Protests at district level, march to Election Commission’s office, rallies, appeal in Supreme Court - all make for good optics, but can they bring about enough pressure?The Congress, which is leading the opposition block, has been consistent in raising these issues, but has failed to keep the momentum going. Rahul Gandhi has addressed several press conferences in the last two years leading the charge against the Election Commission and Gyanesh Kumar. His yatra in Bihar ahead of assembly elections last year brought the issue to centre stage but once again the momentum did not sustain.Clearly, the Congress and the other opposition parties need to think how to run a sustained campaign for mobilisation.At the CWC meeting held on Tuesday, ahead of today’s INDIA bloc meeting, Rahul Gandhi had claimed that revelations about the Election Commission were now coming out in the open because of the Congress. During the two-and-a-half hour CWC meeting, Rahul pointed out that the Congress had been raising the "vote chori" issue strongly with facts and talked about irregularities in polls in Haryana, Karnataka and Maharashtra but many were sceptical of it.Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha claimed that EVM and voters' list "match-fixing" of polls was underway in the country and asserted that his party should not budge from the path of "virodh" (opposing) as well as "pratirodh" (resistance) against it from streets to Parliament.Rahul Verma, political scientist and a Fellow at New Delhi-based think tank Centre for Policy Research, feels that the Congress needs to be persistent and have patience.“One of the reasons why the congress fails to do mobilization is that they raise important issues but are not persistent. They need to have patience. Congress has been talking about all the important issues but did not sit on a protest like the CJP,” Rahul Verma says.“Even the CJP would not have thought of the success they eventually got. They continued sitting on protest even when there was little traction in their favour. Eventually, they managed to mobilise a lot of support and forced the government to concede to their demands,” Rahul Verma adds.If the INDIA bloc meeting was about showcasing opposition unity, well the purpose was at best half achieved. There were more questions on INDIA bloc’s united presence than answers. The BJP has aggressively highlighted the division within the opposition ranks. With several regional parties openly against the Congress, the BJP leaders have been quick to question Rahul Gandhi’s acceptance as the leader of the opposition block.BJP national media incharge Ashish Usha Agarwal questioned Rahul Gandhi’s leadership of the INDIA bloc and said the outcomes of the INDIA bloc meeting on Wednesday were "zero vision, 100 per cent frustration.The BJP claimed that the meeting was an advance excuse for poll defeats, with the leaders of the opposition grouping rejecting Rahul Gandhi's leadership."The INDI Alliance fell apart even before the meeting took place. The DMK did not attend the meeting. Akhilesh was busy elsewhere. The AAP had already declined," Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan said at a press conference at the BJP headquarters.“Why is this happening? It is because the INDI Alliance is simply not willing to accept Rahul Gandhi as its leader. His leadership is not being accepted; that is why they are not even showing up," Chouhan said, contending that Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav would have come to attend the meeting if it was "really so important."Chouhan claimed that the opposition INDIA bloc is crumbling. "No matter how many times they (Congress) try to re-launch Rahul Gandhi, the INDIA bloc does not consider him their leader," he said.Clearly, the opposition needs to do things differently. When Mamata Banerjee said the opposition had taken these matters to the Election Commission and the Supreme Court and "knocked on every possible door," it was an admission of the fact that the old ways had failed. The meeting today discussed the need for mobilisation on the ground by involving the civil society along with the political fight.The Congress has kept an arm’s distance from the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP). But perhaps it is time for the Congress to course correct and take a leaf out of the CJP’s successful mobilisation programme.

Musa’s neutralisation blow to LeT network

SRINAGAR/ NEW DELHI: In a joint operation by Army, police and security forces, a top Pakistani Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist, identified as Mohammad Asif, alias Hashim Musa, was killed in an overnight encounter in the upper reaches of Yousmarg, around 60km from Srinagar.With his elimination, the entire group of four LeT commanders who had been operating in J&K since 2022 and were also behind the Pahalgam massacre has been wiped out. Home ministry called it a massive victory. Intelligence agencies had been tracking for two years the whereabouts of this former Pak Special Service Group (SSG) commando who had infiltrated into the Valley.Neutralisation of Musa is a serious blow to LeT ecosystem in J&K,” the ministry said in a statement. This group was responsible for a string of sensational and deadly attacks across the region. The Musa-led squad’s terror trail included the Kandi attack in Rajouri (May 2023) where five Army personnel were killed, the Halan attack (Aug 2023), and the Dera Ki Gali ambush (Dec 2023) where terrorists targeted two Army vehicles, killing several soldiers.The group also orchestrated the June 9, 2024 attack on a bus carrying Hindu pilgrims in Reasi, killing nine and wounding 40. They were linked to the Oct 2024 Gagangir attack in Ganderbal, which claimed the lives of seven, and the Bootapathri attack near Gulmarg that killed two soldiers and two civilians. The violent spree culminated in the devastating April 2025 Baisaran Valley attack in Pahalgam, where the terrorists massacred 26 tourists and a local horseman.
Article Summary: A top pakistani lashkar-e-taiba terrorist, identified as mohammad asif, alias hashim musa, was killed in an overnight encounter in the upper reaches of yousmarg. The entire group of four let commanders who had been operating in j&k since 2022 and were also behind the pahalgam massacre has been wiped out.

PM Narendra Modi held a phone call with US President Donald Trump Wednesday to review bilateral cooperation in trade, defence, critical technologies and energy, amid increasing friction in the relationship driven primarily by India’s purchase of Russian oil.Modi is learnt to have touched upon India’s concerns related to the US’ latest Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 (SRIA) that allows the president to impose up to 100 percent tariffs on countries like India and China for their procurement of Russian oil.In the run up to the Modi-Trump conversation – their first since they met in France in June – both external affairs minister S Jaishankar and foreign secretary Vikram Misri had flagged the same concerns with American authorities, emphasising the recently enacted SRIA would have consequences for India-US ties. India continues to maintain that its energy sourcing is driven by national interests and the need to ensure reliable and affordable supplies for 1.4 billion people.Modi said in a post on X that he had productive conversation with Trump. “We reviewed our bilateral cooperation in trade, defence, energy, critical technologies and other areas. We agreed to maintain close engagement to take our Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership forward,” said the PM, adding that they also exchanged views on regional and international issues, including ongoing efforts to advance global peace and security.An Indian readout said they agreed to maintain close engagement to deepen cooperation for the benefit of the people of both countries, and also to remain in touch. There was no White House readout till late in the evening.According to diplomatic sources, the conversation helped reinforce the strategic partnership amid the friction over the US passage of the Russia-related legislation, and also differences over trade that have prevented the 2 countries from concluding a bilateral trade agreement. Modi will travel to the US in December for the G20 summit in Florida where he is likely to also have a bilateral meeting with Trump. Earlier this week, foreign secretary Vikram Misri told a visiting Congressional delegation that the new law will have a negative impact on not just bilateral relations but also the energy situation in global markets.Trade and energy, however, are not the only issues that India and the US need to address to get the relationship back on track. Article Title: Operation Sheruwali: How security forces tracked LeT commander Musa in months-long hunt since May
Article Text:
Hashim Moosa (Left) killed in an encounter in Jammu and Kashmir’s Budgam district, Indian Army (File photo)

How Operation Sheruwali unfolded

Is Hashim Moosa an ex-Pakistan SSG commando?

Four-member LeT group neutralised

The three other commanders were killed in separate encounters:

Junaid Bhat: Neutralised on December 3, 2024, in Dachigam.

Suleman: Killed on July 28, 2025, during Operation Mahadev.

Musa's alleged role in Pahalgam attack

NEW DELHI: The killing of senior Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) commander Mohammad Asif alias Hashim Musa in Jammu and Kashmir's Budgam district on Wednesday was the culmination of a months-long intelligence-led operation, named ‘Operation Sheruwali’, launched in May 2026.Security forces had been tracking Musa for a prolonged period before a coordinated plan involving multiple agencies was drawn up to neutralise him, following the receipt of technical and human intelligence about his movements and presence in the area.The operation culminated in an encounter in the Yousmarg area of Budgam, where Musa was killed. His body was later recovered along with war-like stores, according to the Army.Also read| Ex-Pakistan SSG commando, highly trained LeT terrorist, Pahalgam mastermind: Who was Hashim Moosa; killed in J&K encounter The ministry of information and broadcasting said the operation dealt a blow to the LeT network in Jammu and Kashmir, with Musa's killing bringing an end to a group of four senior commanders who had been operating in the union territory since 2022 and were linked to several attacks.According to a statement issued by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), security forces had been pursuing Musa for a long time.A specific plan involving all stakeholders was recently put in place after intelligence inputs indicated his movement and presence.The government said the operation to neutralise Musa was part of the ongoing ‘Operation Sheruwali’, which began in May 2026.The Army's Chinar Corps, meanwhile, said the encounter took place during Operation Korag in the Yousmarg area of Budgam district. Troops launched a search operation based on specific intelligence inputs and challenged suspicious movement, following which terrorists opened fire.The operation involved the Indian Army, Jammu and Kashmir Police and the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF).The search continued after the encounter, with security personnel checking the surrounding areas for any additional terrorist presence. Musa's body was recovered from the general area of Palmaidan along with war-like stores, according to the Chinar Corps.One of the key aspects of Musa's background is his alleged association with Pakistan's military.ANI, quoting security agency sources, reported that Musa had served as a para-commando in Pakistan's Special Service Group (SSG), where he held the rank of Havildar. According to the sources, he retired from the SSG in 2023, subsequently joined the LeT and infiltrated into India.Former Jammu and Kashmir DGP S P Vaid described Musa as a highly trained commando specialising in ambushes and guerrilla-style attacks.Vaid alleged that Musa's footprints had been seen in several attacks in Jammu and Kashmir, including those in Poonch, DKG, Bhimber Gali, Gulmarg and the attack on pilgrims in Reasi.However, his alleged military background has been reported by security agency sources and has not been independently established.With Musa's killing, all four senior LeT commanders belonging to the group that had been active in Jammu and Kashmir since 2022 have been neutralised, according to the government.The government linked the group to several attacks across Jammu and Kashmir, including the Halan attack in August 2023, DKG attack in December 2023, Kandi attack in May 2023, Shahsitar attack in May 2024, Shiv Khori attack in June 2024, Gagangir and Bootapathri attacks in October 2024, and the Baisaran attack in April 2025.Musa was among the key suspects in the April 22, 2025, Pahalgam terror attack , in which terrorists targeted tourists at Baisaran Valley, killing 26 people.The Jammu and Kashmir Police had announced a reward of Rs 20 lakh for information leading to the arrest of Pakistan nationals and LeT terrorists Adil Hussain Thoker, Ali Bhai and Hashim Musa.The National Investigation Agency (NIA) subsequently chargesheeted seven accused in the case, including Pakistan-based LeT and The Resistance Front (TRF), which it accused of planning, facilitating and executing the attack.The NIA's 1,597-page chargesheet also named Pakistani handler Sajid Jatt as an accused and detailed the alleged Pakistan-based conspiracy behind the attack.The government said the operation reflected sustained coordination between the Jammu and Kashmir Police, the Indian Army and Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) in counter-terrorism operations across the union territory.
Article Summary: Hashim moosa killed in an encounter in jammu and kashmir’s budgam district, indian army. Security forces had been tracking musa for a prolonged period before a coordinated plan involving multiple agencies was drawn up to neutralise him. His body was later recovered along with war-like stores.

Article Title: 'No ban but also not 24x7': SC on firecrackers in Delhi-NCR ahead of Diwali
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Wednesday said it would not impose a blanket ban on firecrackers in Delhi-NCR, but would also not permit fireworks throughout the day, saying a balance had to be struck between public health concerns and people’s sentiments.A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale said the court would consider allowing firecrackers only during specified hours."We will make it very clear. Neither we are going to agree for total ban, nor are we going to allow them to do it (fireworks) for 24 hours a day. Total ban will affect sentiments. And allowing them throughout the day will have huge impact on every other living being including the old, sick and children," the bench orally observed, as quoted by PTI."We need to find a solution by which we can give a specified time," it added.The observations came during a hearing in which the Centre proposed a limited relaxation for a category of next-generation joined green crackers developed with technical inputs from the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research-National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (CSIR-NEERI).Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati submitted a note saying the court could consider permitting the specified green crackers subject to conditions on their manufacture, chemical composition, noise levels and emissions.According to the note, only duly licensed manufacturers would be allowed to produce the crackers. They would also have to meet the prescribed noise limit of 125 dB(AI)/145 dB(C) peak and could not contain banned chemicals.The proposed crackers are linked or joined fireworks formulated with reduced quantities of barium salts, with the aim of lowering emissions. The proposal is based on the category recommended by CSIR-NEERI and would be subject to applicable safety, noise and emission standards.The bench further said it would consider the issue concerning the use of barium in firecrackers on October 15.The court's latest observations come ahead of Diwali and follow its earlier orders regulating the manufacture, sale and use of firecrackers in Delhi and the National Capital Region.Last year, the Supreme Court allowed the sale and use of green firecrackers in Delhi-NCR subject to conditions, including restrictions on when they could be used.The court had said their use would be limited to specified hours on the days before Diwali and on Diwali itself, as part of measures aimed at balancing festival-related celebrations with concerns over air pollution and public health.

MEA warns against joining Russian forces

India continues talks with Russia

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs has issued a fresh advisory cautioning Indians against joining the Russian armed forces, warning of the “mortal dangers” involved and urging citizens to exercise due diligence when considering job offers in Russia.The advisory, issued on Wednesday, comes amid continued reports of Indian nationals being recruited into the Russian military.The government said it has repeatedly highlighted the risks involved and urged Indians not to be lured by unverified employment offers.The MEA said some Indian nationals have willingly sought offers to join the Russian armed forces in the expectation of receiving monetary benefits and later securing their release with the help of the Indian government.“It is reiterated that this is a dangerous path and is strongly discouraged by the Government,” the advisory said.The ministry also said there had been “numerous instances” of individuals approaching Indian authorities to voluntarily give up their Indian citizenship, obtain a Russian passport and subsequently join the Russian armed forces.Some individuals, it said, had already taken such steps without consulting Indian authorities after being attracted by temporary financial benefits.“It is advised that individuals should consider the gravity of such actions and understand the mortal dangers they are exposing themselves to,” the MEA said, advising Indian nationals to refrain from taking such actions.The government also cautioned Indians about recruitment by non-public entities, including voluntary groups, saying foreign nationals were being recruited to serve in the Russian armed forces through such organisations.The MEA advised Indians to exercise due diligence before accepting job offers from agents that are not registered with the ministry of external affairs.The government said it remains engaged with Russia to ensure the safety, well-being and early discharge of all Indian nationals serving in the country's armed forces.The latest advisory follows figures shared by foreign secretary Vikram Misri last month. Misri said 227 Indian nationals had been recruited into the Russian armed forces, of whom 139 had been discharged and 51 had died.Misri said India had raised the issue with Russia “at various levels on various occasions” and remained in constant discussions with Moscow for the early discharge and repatriation of those whose cases were still pending.He also said the Indian Embassy in Moscow was regularly monitoring the situation and working with Russian authorities to facilitate the release and return of the remaining Indian nationals.The MEA's latest advisory reiterated that engagement with the Russian side would continue to secure the safety and early discharge of Indian nationals serving in the Russian armed forces.
Article Summary: The advisory, issued on wednesday, comes amid continued reports of indian nationals being recruited into the russian military. The government said it has repeatedly highlighted the risks involved and urged indians not to be lured by unverified employment offers.

NEW DELHI: India's consul general in Shanghai Pratik Mathur on Wednesday met Shanghai Mayor Zhu Zhongming and conveyed New Delhi's greetings ahead of the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China.The consulate general of India in Shanghai shared images of celebrations marking Guo Qing Jie, or National Day, in Shanghai in a post on X."Consul General Shri Pratik Mathur conveyed our best wishes to Shanghai Mayor HE Zhu Zhongming on Guo Qing Jie, the 77th anniversary of the founding of the PRC," the consulate said.Zhu is among the first leaders born in the 1970s to serve as Shanghai mayor, a position held by several Chinese leaders who later rose to the Politburo. NEW DELHI: Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) terrorist Mohammad Asif alias Hashim Moosa, wanted for his alleged role in the 2025 Pahalgam terror attack , was killed in an encounter with security forces in Jammu and Kashmir's Budgam district on Wednesday.Moosa was killed during a joint operation by the Indian Army , Jammu and Kashmir Police and the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) in the Korag area of Yousmarg. His body was later recovered from the general area of Palmaidan along with war-like stores, according to the Army's Chinar Corps.Moosa's killing has brought renewed focus on the background of the LeT terrorist, who security agencies had identified as one of the key suspects in the Pahalgam attack and linked to other terror attacks in Jammu and Kashmir.Moosa was a Pakistani LeT terrorist wanted in connection with the April 22, 2025 Pahalgam terror attack, in which 26 people were killed.Former Jammu and Kashmir DGP S.P. Vaid on Wednesday described Moosa as a highly trained terrorist and alleged that his footprints had surfaced in several attacks in Jammu and Kashmir, including attacks in the Poonch region and the Pahalgam attack.Vaid said Moosa was considered the mastermind of the Pahalgam attack and described him as a Pakistani national and a commando-trained terrorist specialising in jungle warfare and guerrilla operations.One of the key aspects of Moosa's background now being examined is his alleged connection with Pakistan's military.News agency ANI also quotes security agency sources stating that Moosa had served as a para-commando in Pakistan's Special Service Group (SSG) where he held the rank of Havildar. Following his retirement from the SSG in 2023, he joined the terrorist outfit Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) and infiltrated into India.Vaid described Moosa as a highly trained commando specialising in ambushes and guerrilla-style attacks. He alleged that Moosa's footprints had been seen in attacks in Poonch, DKG, Bhimber Gali, the Gulmarg attack and the Reasi attack on pilgrims.The alleged SSG connection could shed further light on Moosa's training and his role within the LeT network, but the military background remains a matter of investigation.ALSO READ: 'Save Democracy March' announced: INDIA bloc projects unity amid SIR row, targets PM Modi, Amit Shah The Pahalgam attack took place on April 22, 2025, when terrorists targeted tourists at Baisaran Valley. Twenty-six people were killed in the attack.According to the ANI report, Moosa was named as one of the key suspects in the attack and had been wanted by Jammu and Kashmir Police.The National Investigation Agency later chargesheeted seven accused in the case, including Pakistan-based LeT and The Resistance Front (TRF), which it charged as a legal entity for allegedly planning, facilitating and executing the attack.The NIA's 1,597-page chargesheet also named Pakistani handler Sajid Jatt as an accused.The agency had said its investigation detailed the Pakistan-based conspiracy and the roles of those accused in the attack.Security forces launched Operation Korag in the Yousmarg area of Budgam following specific intelligence inputs about terrorist movement.During the joint search operation, troops observed suspicious activity and challenged the terrorists. The terrorists opened fire, triggering an encounter in which Moosa was killed.The operation involved the Indian Army, Jammu and Kashmir Police and the CRPF.The search operation continued after the encounter, with security personnel checking the surrounding area for any additional terrorist presence. During the search, Moosa's body was recovered from Palmaidan along with war-like stores, according to the Chinar Corps.The killing also drew a reaction from Asavari Jagdale, daughter of Pahalgam attack victim Santosh Jagdale.Speaking to ANI, Jagdale thanked the Army and intelligence agencies for the operation and recalled the April 22 attack in which 26 people were killed.She described the killing as a step towards justice but said the legal process must continue until the case reaches its final verdict.“I would say that one chapter of the case has ended,” she said.Jagdale also urged security agencies to continue operations against terrorists and said the 26 families would consider the case fully closed only after completion of the legal proceedings.
